data.why: The old gas station layout: the tank in the pit under the sidewalk, the fill pipe on the left; the fuel's path from the delivery at the fill pipe into the tank, its walls and the gap, and out as fumes through a vent; a station worker watches each step.

story.title: How a Gas Station Tank Works

chain.shows: fuel spills at the fill pipe
an overfill gushes past the bucket
the steel tank rusts and leaks into the groundwater
a leak hides between the walls
fumes puff out at the fill pipe

surprises.claim: A spill bucket around the fill pipe catches fuel spilled during a delivery.
surprises.search: UST spill bucket fill pipe catches drips delivery

surprises.claim: An overfill valve in the fill pipe shuts off the flow when the tank is nearly full.
surprises.search: overfill prevention valve fill pipe shuts off flow tank full

surprises.claim: Double-walled tanks have a gap between the walls that is monitored for leaks.
surprises.search: double walled underground storage tank interstitial monitoring sensor

surprises.claim: Underground fuel tanks have vent pipes that release vapors above the ground.
surprises.search: underground storage tank vent pipe vapors height

ideas.idea: the pit is dug, a steel tank appears and fills with amber gasoline
dark fuel runs down beside the fill pipe
a black spill bucket appears round the top of the fill pipe and the spill stops
fuel gushes up out of the full fill pipe onto the sidewalk
a red valve appears in the fill pipe and the gushing stops
drips fall from the tank and dark fuel seeps down into the groundwater
a green fiberglass second wall appears round the tank and the leak stops
amber fuel collects in the gap between the two walls
a sensor appears in the gap and its red light flashes
an underground storage tank with two walls, a sensor and a spill bucket
gasoline fumes puff out of the fill pipe
a tall vent pipe rises and the fumes drift out at its top
a concrete cover slides over the pit, a fuel pump appears and the worker walks to it
a car pulls in beside the pump over the finished tank

sentences.text: If you bury a tank of gasoline, you have a gas station tank.
But fuel spills at the fill pipe.
So you add a spill bucket around it.
But an overfill gushes past the bucket.
So a valve shuts when the tank is nearly full.
But the steel tank rusts and leaks.
So you wrap it in a second wall.
But a leak between the walls stays hidden.
So a sensor in the gap flashes an alarm.
This is an underground storage tank.
But fumes still puff out past the sensor.
So a tall vent pipe lets them out up high.
Bury the tank, pour the cover, and fill your car.
Congratulations, you have built a gas station tank.
